name: Two-by-Three Endpoint-Cover Obstruction
statement: Let $X=P\mathbin{\dot\cup}Q$ with $|P|=2$ and $|Q|=3$, and let $\mathcal H\subseteq2^X$ be union closed and well graded, with at most eleven states, no empty state, and a complementary pair $A,B$. There cannot simultaneously be an absent state whose two $P$-neighbors are present and lie in the required $A$-outward directions, and an absent state whose three $Q$-neighbors are present and has at least two required $B$-outward directions.
proof: The two holes force punctured coordinate subcubes inside $\mathcal H$. Union closure, the endpoint directions, absence of the two holes, and the order bound reduce the possibilities to fourteen symmetry orbits. Ten order-eleven cases violate well-gradedness directly. In each of the four order-ten cases, no single additional state can repair all missing tight paths.
